newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - June T-bonds reject upper end of range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - June T-bonds reject upper end of range.

text.p: U.S. June T-bond futures were lower after rejecting the upper end of a 2-1/2 week range in early pit trade, technical analysts said.
"We will probably be in a range through the week," said David Ging, Treasury market strategist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.
June T-bonds failed for the second day in a row to test the 2-1/2 week high of 107-28/32 in reaction to weak U.S. economic numbers.
Some floor traders thought U.S. March housing starts data could be the catalyst to push June to 108-00.
Housing starts fell to an annual rate of 1.425 million units, compared with average trade estimates of 1.46 million units and against February's downward revised rate of 1.522 million.
June T-bonds rebounded to 107-27/32 on Tuesday, but were unable to even retest the overnight high of 107-23/32 after U.S. housing starts data on Wednesday morning.
"What that is telling you is that yesterday was probably just a short squeeze," said Nick Kalivas, senior credit market analyst at Refco Inc.
However, total open interest for bond futures was estimated to have risen more than 18,000 contracts on Tuesday, sparking ideas that any short-covering was offset by new short positions.
Open interest for September Eurodollars also rose on Tuesday, up more than 12,000.
During Tuesday's rebound, many traders and analysts speculated that shorts were exiting or covering positions, especially since the core U.S. consumer price index on Tuesday rose less than expected.
"The fact that the market had been preparing for a higher core CPI number forced a lot of people out," Kalivas said.
"But then the conclusion you can draw (from open interest) is that a lot of shorts were established at the highs," he said. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
